subject: Tenant security handover — SSO/SCIM, IP allowlist and service account sequencing

Subject: Tenant security handover — prep for SSO/SCIM & IP allowlist

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're planning a controlled production onboarding window for our Redwood tenant and need a short security handoff so our infra team can sign off. Key asks:

- Confirm SSO metadata and IdP cert exchange process (we use Okta)
- SCIM provisioning: which attributes Redwood expects for groups/users and the token rotation cadence
- IP allowlist ranges Redwood will call from and whether a stable egress CIDR bundle is available for our firewall team
- Service accounts for SCIM and KV-cache webhook access: required scopes and recommended naming scheme
- Any org-policy flags we need to set on our side (provider-level RBAC, session length, device trust)

We're aiming for a canary on 2027-09-20 and full cutover 2027-09-22 (US-PST maintenance windows). Can you confirm who from Redwood will own the cutover runbook and whether you can provide a rollback plan?

I'll attach our SAML metadata and a provisional SCIM token to this thread for your engineers to validate.

Thanks,
Aisha Malik
Director of Infrastructure
FinProspect, Inc.

Attachments: finprospect-saml-metadata.xml (xml), finprospect-scim-token.txt (text)
From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Tenant security handover — prep for SSO/SCIM & IP allowlist

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear list. We're aligned to support the timeline and I can own the orchestration and runbook on the Redwood side. High-level answers below; Jonas and Ben will follow up with config-level details and an explicit cutover checklist.

Quick answers:
- SSO (SAML): we accept SAML 2.0 metadata upload via Console and via API. We'll need Identity Provider metadata and the signing certificate (X.509). If Okta is the IdP, send the metadata XML; we'll generate SP metadata and certificate to return.
- SCIM: Redwood expects SCIM 2.0 with users and groups endpoints. Required user attrs: userName, name.familyName, name.givenName, emails[type="work"].value, active (boolean). Groups should include displayName and members (value=user id). We'll supply example mappings and a test harness.
- IP allowlist: we publish a stable egress CIDR bundle for production; I'll attach the current ranges in the cutover diagram PDF. We also support a short-lived tunneling option if your firewall team prefers ephemeral exceptions.
- Service accounts: create two SAs in your tenant: redwood-scim-provisioner and redwood-webhook. SCIM needs bearer token with provisioning scope (user:write, group:write). Webhook needs a keypair for HMAC verification. We'll provide naming conventions and minimal privileges.
- Org policies: ensure your Okta org allows SP-initiated SSO for the Redwood SP, allow group pushes from SCIM, and avoid strict IP restrictions on the SCIM outbound calls to Redwood (we'll instead restrict inbound access on our side).

Action items I own:
1) Produce cutover runbook + rollback steps (will attach by EOD 2027-09-13)
2) Publish egress CIDR bundle (attached as cutover-sequence-diagram.pdf)
3) Provide SCIM attribute mapping examples and test harness credentials (Jonas)

Jonas — will you validate the SCIM mapping and confirm rate limiting guidance? Ben — can you draft the runbook with the step-by-step checks we need during canary?

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Technical Account Lead | Redwood Inference

Hi Aisha, Stephanie — quick technical follow-up from our infra/security side. I'm attaching an internal SCIM mapping sample in the Drive link; below are the specifics FinProspect's IdP/provisioner should align to.

SCIM specifics (summary):
- Token: please provide a bearer token for the scim-provisioner account; token format is standard Bearer; we recommend TTL of 90 days and a documented rotation process. Do not embed tokens in automation without vaulting.
- Batch size & rate limiting: Redwood SCIM accepts batches up to 200 members per request; we throttle at 10 reqs/sec for provisioning endpoints. If you plan a bulk sync, reach out and we'll open a temporary higher throughput window.
- Attribute mapping: include externalId on users for idempotency; use emails[0].value as canonical email. For groups, include members as references to externalId.
- SCIM endpoints: https://scim.redwood.example/v2/Users and /Groups — TLS 1.2+.

IP egress notes:
- Production egress CIDRs (current): 34.201.0.0/16, 52.12.128.0/18, 3.94.64.0/18 (will be in the attached PDF). We'll announce any changes at least 14 days in advance.
- If your firewall requires a single IP, we can arrange a static NAT for the session but it requires support ticket and 24hr notice.

Service account scopes:
- redwood-scim-provisioner: scim:users:write, scim:groups:write (no admin UI scope)
- redwood-webhook: webhook:deliver, webhook:read (HMAC verification keypair stored in your KMS)

I'll add the mapping examples to the shared Drive and post a short postman collection for testing.

—Jonas
Senior Security Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: cutover-sequence-diagram.pdf (diagram of egress ranges and cutover windows)

Hi Rahul/Aisha — confirmed. Redwood will staff the two maintenance windows and I'll be primary runbook lead during the canary. Answers inline: 

1) SCIM preview/dry-run: yes — we support a preview mode in which we validate payloads and report delta actions without applying them. We'll enable preview for the canary by default.
2) Staffing: Ben Carter (runbook lead), Stephanie Nguyen (program manager), Jonas Weber (security/SCIM), plus on-call infra as backup. We'll run the canary, validate logs/metrics, and only flip the provisioning toggle during confirmed windows.
3) Rollback: our rollback plan includes immediate disabling of the SCIM API key, reverting group mappings with a stored snapshot, and a staged rollback of SSO DNS/SP metadata if session issues appear. We'll publish the full step-by-step runbook (with exact curl commands and KMS key names) to the Drive link by 2027-09-15 18:00 PST.

- Stephanie: attach runbook draft and postman collection (EOD 2027-09-13) — IN PROGRESS
